subject: Future Tech
title: The History of AI Winters
description: A 60-second lesson on The History of AI Winters.

hook.text: Twice, AI hype collapsed into 'AI winters'—decades where funding vanished and researchers fled the field.

buildup.text: In the 1960s, scientists promised human-level AI within 20 years.

discovery.text: The second winter hit in the late 1980s when expert systems—hand-coded rules—proved too brittle for real-world problems.

twist.text: Each winter killed hype but not progress.

climax.text: Deep learning's 2012 breakthrough ended the last winter. Now AI investment exceeds $100 billion yearly.

punchline.text: AI has died twice and risen twice. The next bet is the biggest.

quiz.question: What caused the first AI winter?
options: Overpromised results led governments to slash funding
